learner_visual_status.note: One true local photo source retained; three explicitly OTHER-species existing photographs are comparison examples. Anatomical micros needed: notched lemma awn, paired glumes, ligule, roots. No new photos added.

best_field_traits: Cool-season ANNUAL, usually 20–60 cm; fibrous rooted, solitary or small tuft, lacking stolons/rhizomes.
Leaves flat and variably hairy, sheaths open, auricles absent; 1–2 mm ragged-edged MEMBRANOUS ligule inside leaf collar.
Slender relatively NARROW panicle with ascending small branches; often appears gently bent or nodding at the tip.
Each ~3–4 mm spikelet contains ONE fertile floret enclosed by TWO firm nearly equal glumes.
Fertile lemma tip has TWO short teeth and ONE often bent/twisted ~8–12 mm awn emerging from the NOTCH between them; verify at 10–20×.
Annual habit, spring bloom or habitat are useful support only; photographs of panicle silhouette alone are NOT species confirmation.
what_to_photograph_for_confirmation: WHOLE ROOTED PLANT: a connected fibrous-rooted tuft with entire narrow seedhead in frame and a 1-cm scale; no stolons or rhizomes.
WHOLE PANICLE: side view from flag leaf through narrowly ascending, sometimes nodding flowering branches with attached mature spikelets.
SPIKELET 10–20×: TWO stiff, subequal, ~3–4 mm glumes surrounding ONE fertile floret, mm ruler for scale.
CRITICAL LEMMA 20×: clearly show two terminal teeth and exactly ONE ~8–12 mm bent/twisted awn originating in notch BETWEEN those teeth.
LEAF COLLAR: turn back the blade and show the actual 1–2 mm ragged-edged membranous ligule with a 1-mm scale.
MATCHED LOOKALIKES: same-scale threeawn three-limbed lemma, lovegrass multifloret spikelet and panicgrass two-floret spikelet.
crew_field_check: OZARKGRASS: find a slender annual tuft with fibrous roots and a relatively NARROW, sometimes slightly nodding spring panicle. At 10–20× inspect ONE ~3–4 mm spikelet: TWO stiff nearly equal glumes enclose ONE fertile floret. The lemma has TWO small apical teeth; its SINGLE 8–12 mm often bent and twisted awn emerges BETWEEN those teeth. A true 1–2 mm membranous, minutely jagged ligule sits inside the blade–sheath junction. Flowerhead silhouette alone is not a confirmed ID; the current photo does NOT prove lemma teeth or ligule.

Aristida threeawns: normally THREE awn limbs arising from ONE lemma, vs Limnodea's single notched-lemma awn. Eragrostis lovegrasses: generally MULTIPLE florets per spikelet, not just one. Panicum (e.g., switchgrass): typically a lower sterile/staminate floret with a hardened fertile UPPER floret rather than one fertile floret with the Limnodea notched awn. Muhlenbergia: can ALSO have one fertile floret, so compare the paired glumes, lemma teeth/awn origin, ligule and annual tuft; panicle openness and one awn alone are insufficient.
Do not call a one-floret airy panicle Limnodea if you cannot see its paired glumes and two-toothed awned lemma. Label provisional grass sp. and collect flowering macro.

measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.look_here_first: Small fibrous-rooted annual with slender contracted panicle; dissect one 3.5–4 mm spikelet. Two stiff subequal glumes enclose a single fertile floret whose TWO-toothed lemma bears ONE often bent awn arising between the teeth.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.growth_form_collar: Annual, approximately 20–60 cm, with no perennial rhizome or rooting stolon; true ligule a short, non-hair-fringed membranous flap, locally reported ~1–2 mm. Confirm exact attached blade/sheath junction.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.spikelet_glumes: Spikelets approximately 3.5–4 mm with one fertile floret and barren rachilla extension. Both stiff, rough, nearly equal glumes generally 3–5-veined and reaching the floret tip (GrassBase genus account). Count veins under transmitted light.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.lemma_palea_awn: Three-veined, keeled fertile lemma with two apical teeth; one subapical often bent/twisted awn arises from between teeth (regional accounts ~5–12 mm). Palea about 0.7× lemma length. Do not mislabel the awn as a glume awn.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.local_lookalikes: Aristida has three awn limbs on one lemma; Eragrostis usually several fertile florets per spikelet; Panicum has a lower sterile/staminate floret and hard upper fertile floret; Muhlenbergia can also be one-flowered, so inspect teeth, glume vein counts and awn insertion.
precise_photo_arrow_gaps: Connected fibrous annual roots and entire narrow panicle with centimeter scale; document flowering season and site without changing native-range status.
Three intact 3.5–4 mm spikelets at 10–20×, both 3–5-veined glumes exposed and measured.
One dissected lemma at 20–40× showing two apical teeth and a single awn emerging BETWEEN them, with 1-mm scale; exact origin must be visible before arrow.
Attached true membranous ligule and same-scale Aristida/Muhlenbergia spikelet comparisons with per-image public-use permissions.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.public_ready_criteria: Preserve original CC BY-NC image, two visible gross arrows and existing scientific holds. Keep FIELD_READY_PHOTO_GAPS until actual measured glumes, lemma teeth/awn origin, collar and rooted annual evidence are taxon-vetted, licensed and public-site QA verified.
measured_diagnostic_key_20261023.source_scope: Kew GrassBase genus account and local Texas species treatment; morphological source measurements not confirmed in existing single overview photograph.
